card.title: PlayStation 5 SSD Controller Current Draw & Fuse F7520 Diagnostics

claims.statement: A working SSD circuit draws 310mA across fuse F7520.
claims.evidence: Measurement across the fuse pads in current mode on a good board.

claims.statement: Remove fuse F7520 that feeds voltage to the voltage regulator generating power for the SSD circuit to measure current draw in series.
claims.evidence: Procedure for isolating and measuring SSD circuit current.
claims.quote: Remove fuse F7520 that feeds the voltage on the back to the voltage regulator that generates power for the SSD circuit. Set a multimeter in current mode in series with the pads of the fuse and measure the current draw.

claims.statement: A standby current draw of 175 mA dropping back to 10 mA can indicate a bad SSD controller IC.
claims.evidence: Current draw profile observed during standby boot sequence.
claims.quote: When you see a current draw in standby of 175 mA and then back to 10Ma. There can be a bad SSD controller IC.

claims.statement: If the current draw is different on a faulty board compared to the expected working value, replace the SSD controller IC.
claims.evidence: Diagnosis based on current draw anomaly across fuse F7520.
claims.quote: If current is different on a faulty board change the SSD controller IC.

procedure: Remove fuse F7520 that feeds voltage to the voltage regulator for the SSD circuit.
Set a multimeter to current mode.
Place the multimeter probes in series with the pads of fuse F7520.
Measure the current draw and compare it against the expected 310mA value.
Replace the SSD controller IC if the measured current draw is abnormal.

measurements.context: Good working SSD circuit current draw

card.caveats: Ensure the meter is wired strictly in series across the fuse pads to avoid shorting or misreading current.
